figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.
figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading). Paper counts come from the maintainer's ledger and undercount some components, notably language models, confirmation and correction.

M01.note: Inherited from the Chang-lab ECoG reading paradigm.

M02.note: Inversion inherited from Chartier et al. 2018 (same lab); slot under-recorded in the ledger.

M03.note: Ordinary per-participant training for invasive decoding.

choice: Applied to 58 mimed trials of 10 sentences (P1)
M04.note: Martin et al. 2014 used the same transfer-and-DTW evaluation in ECoG (covert silent reading rather than miming); mimed values are in figures only.

M05.note: Standard clinical ECoG features of the lineage.

M06.note: No earlier example found (recall estimate 0.74), but the gain is shown in one participant with no stated repetition, and a later linear study found direct decoding slightly better, so not ahead.

M07.field: No language model or lexicon at use time
M07.note: Direct acoustic synthesis needs no language model.

M08.note: Guenther 2009 and Martin 2014 preceded it; sentence waveforms with listener tests are the addition.

M11.note: Split by recording session; Fig. 1 caption mentions 5-fold cross-validation inconsistently.

M12.field: Listener intelligibility tests of synthesized speech
M12.note: Listener tests were established practice; chance-level WER for the word pools is not given.
